params.place: on the map: the Ural Mountains, a small Russia to their west

moments.what: Russia's small red shape west of the mountains traces in light
its east edge stops in a hard line
the Ural ridge rises along the line
URAL MOUNTAINS writes along the ridge
a Cossack boat pushes off east from the ridge
the camera pulls back east across empty Siberia
the Pacific coast glows far to the right and a question mark drops on it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Russia once ended at the Ural Mountains. So how did it reach the Pacific?

params.place: on the map: Siberia, east of the Urals

moments.what: the camera glides east over the ridge
SIBERIA writes across the land
frost spreads over the rivers
pine trees pop up across the map
the pines spread out to the edges of the map
a gold measuring line stretches east from the Urals
the line runs on to the Pacific shore
the coast flashes at the end of the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Beyond them lay Siberia, a frozen forest so wide it ran all the way to the far side of Asia.

params.place: on the map: the Ural pass, the rivers on its eastern side

moments.what: a Cossack in a red coat stands in the bow of a boat at the ridge
YERMAK labels him
the boat climbs over the ridge
the oars dip
men haul the boat on logs over the pass
more boats follow in a line
a banner on the sail shows the number of men

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then a Cossack chief called Yermak crossed them, rowing and dragging river boats, with just 540 men.

params.place: on the map: from the Stroganovs' lands on the Kama to Sibir on the Irtysh

moments.what: a merchant in a fur hat stands west of the Urals
STROGANOVS labels his lands
a bag of coins flies to the boats
the boats row down the river east
the khan's walled town on the Irtysh is reached
a red banner is planted on it
SIBIR writes over it and red spreads to it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: A rich merchant family, the Stroganovs, paid for the trip, and Yermak took the capital of the Khan of Sibir.

params.place: on the map: the forest by the Irtysh, a route back to Moscow

moments.what: a question mark pulses over the forest
the camera pushes into the trees
a pile of furs bursts out of the trees
a dark sable pelt pops up
an orange fox pelt pops beside it
coins rain on the pile
the pelts fly along a route west to Moscow

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But what were they really after? Fur. Sable and fox pelts sold for a fortune in Moscow.

params.place: on the map: a riverbank in western Siberia, Tobolsk

moments.what: a village of tents sits by the river
a boat lands beside it
a sack of furs walks from the village
a YASAK sign stamps on the sack
a Cossack strides in from the right, an axe raised
logs drop onto the bank
the log walls and tower stand up as a fort
the furs pile up inside and red spreads round the fort

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So every village they reached paid a tax in furs, called yasak, and each time the Cossacks built a wooden fort to collect it.

params.place: on the map: the Ob, the Yenisei and the Lena across Siberia

moments.what: the camera pulls back over all of Siberia
the Ob traces in blue and a fort pops on it
the Yenisei traces and a fort pops on it
the Lena traces and a fort pops on it
men drag a boat over land between rivers
red spreads east from fort to fort
a new fort pops at the red front
the red front flashes and races on
a boat shoots off east from the newest fort

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How far could that go? Up the Ob, across to the Yenisei, on to the Lena, dragging the boats from river to river, and every new fort became the start of the next run.

params.place: on the map: hunters' camps along the Lena and across the taiga

moments.what: hunters' camps light up across the forest
families stand by their tents with reindeer
their camps glow warm on the map
a fur is handed over to a Cossack
a hunter raises a bow at the fort
the light goes cold and the camps dim under the red

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The people already living there, Siberia's native peoples, were made to pay, and many who fought back were crushed.

params.place: on the map: the shore of the Sea of Okhotsk, the Pacific

moments.what: the red race line runs on across the last mountains
Yermak's first boat glows far back at the Urals
the Ural ridge flashes
Cossacks walk onto the beach
they stop at the water's edge
waves break and red reaches the coast
a red banner is planted at the edge of the ocean

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And just one lifetime after Yermak crossed the Urals, Cossacks stood on the shore of the Pacific.

params.place: on the map: the whole of Russia from the Baltic to the Pacific

moments.what: the camera pulls back across the continent
fur pelts flicker along the rivers
Russia's whole border traces in light
the flag fills Russia
BIGGEST COUNTRY writes across it
the camera rests on the whole country
a pin drops on the Baltic coast
a pin drops on the Pacific coast and a line joins them

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That race for fur is most of why Russia is now the biggest country on Earth, stretching from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific.

params.place: on the map: back at the Urals

moments.what: a fur pelt pops on the left
a gold bar pops on the right
both glow over the map
a comment bubble pops between the fur and the gold
the bubble drops down and the camera starts gliding west
the camera glides back to the Urals
three boats appear at the ridge
the oars dip and the boats move
the red shrinks back west of the Urals

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Fur or gold: which built more empires? Tell me below. And it all started with a few boats, rowing east from the place where
